result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers reply directly to the hero-stat and big-card idea and keep the summary to a slim strip. B is stronger: it keeps every card the same size, uses color only for exceptions, lets lane position show status, and plans for an uneven split such as 25 trucks in Waiting. A brings back larger type for exception rows and gives every row a green/amber/red bar, which makes routine rows less quiet and works against its own goal of reducing overwhelm. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A firmly rejects the hero stat and the large cards. It shows every truck in five uniform status lanes, keeps colour for exceptions only (a coloured edge on cards past their target time), and plans for an uneven split such as 25 trucks waiting. B also argues well, with pixel maths, stable ordering and status shown by position and shape. But its green/amber/red time bar on every row makes normal rows noisy, and mixing door tiles with lists and a larger-type exception band makes alignment less consistent.
